### Changes Reasoning
Robin implemented the INR currency formatting request by adding Indian Rupee values to the data structure and updating the home page display. The changes involved: 1) Adding 'inr' properties to all order amount objects in the data file with appropriately converted values using the ₹ symbol, 2) Updating the home page table to display INR amounts instead of USD amounts by changing the TableCell content from 'US{order.amount.usd}' to '{order.amount.inr}'. The conversion rates used approximate values of 1 USD ≈ 83 INR for consistency.

### Potential Issues
1) The INR conversion rates are hardcoded approximations and may not reflect real-time exchange rates, 2) Individual order pages may still display USD/CAD amounts creating inconsistency, 3) The change affects all users globally rather than being locale-specific, 4) No TypeScript type updates were made to reflect the new 'inr' property in the amount interface.

### Test Suggestions
1) Verify the home page displays INR amounts correctly with proper ₹ symbol formatting, 2) Check that all order rows show the expected INR values, 3) Test the order detail pages to ensure they still function properly, 4) Validate that the table remains properly aligned with INR amounts, 5) Test responsive behavior on different screen sizes to ensure INR amounts don't break layout.
